textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. Muscle that in respiration in frog is …………. a. sternohyal muscle b. diaphragm c. lingual muscle d. petrohyal muscle and sternohyal muscle 2. Buccopharyngeal cavity communicates with the respiratory tract posteriorly by ………. a. External nares b. glottis c. gullet d. internal nares 3. Which of the following structure is absent in the lung of frog? a. Broncus b. bronchiole c. lungs d. vocal cord 4. Carbon dioxide is the byproduct of cellular respiration that should be eliminated from the body. Which of the following statement best describes the form of which most of the carbondioxide is transported from tissues to the lungs via blood? a. In dissolved form with plasma b. Bound to haemoglobin as carbaminohaemoglobin c. Transported as bicarbonates d. In RBC as carbonic acid 5. Oxygen diffuses through the respiratory surface and enters blood stream which is then transported to various tissues of the body. In which form majority oxygen is transported by blood? a. Haemoglobin combines with oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin b. In the form of bicarbonates c. Oxyen dissolves in plasma and transported d. In RBC as carbonic acid 6. Hibernation and aestivation are the remarkable physiological adaptation shown by frogs to survive in extreme environmental condition such as extreme cold and hot. During such period of inactivity, which type of respiration mainly supports frog? a. branchial respiration b. cutaneous respiration c. pulmonary respiration d. buccal respiration 7. In the process of buccal inspiration, air is drawn into the buccal cavity and for this the floor of buccal cavity undergoes some specific movement. Such movement is essential for creating pressure difference which is for inflow of air. What is the action of floor of buccal cavity at this time? a. Floor of buccal cavity raised up to increase buccal volume Biology, Grade 11 | 421

b. Floor of buccal cavity lowered down for increasing buccal volume c. Floor of buccal cavity lowered down for decreasing buccal volume d. Such mode of respiration is made possible by certain specialities of frog’s skin. Which of the following best explains why cutaneous respiration is feasible in frog? a. The group of organs concerned for producing offspring for the continuation of the generation constitutes reproductive system. Frog is unisexual animal where well marked sexual dimorphism especially in breeding season is found.
Activity: 8.13 Objective: To identify the reproductive organs in frog.

Apparatus required: dissecting tray, forcep, needle, blade, magnifying glass Procedure: i. Lay down a chloroformed or freshly preserved frog in dissecting dish ventro-dorsally i.e. ventral surface facing upwards. ii. Fix the frog by pinning through the limbs. iii. Dissect open the body cavity and remove alimentary canal. iv. Observe kidney which is either with oval shaped testis or with irregular ovary on the either side of vertebral column. v. Identify other organs associated with reproduction (take help of your teacher if required) vi. Draw labeled diagram of reproductive system and discuss. Conclusion:
a) Testes: Testes are paired, oval, yellowish coloured structures. Each testis is attached on the anteroventral surface of the kidney with the help of a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium.
